Class SlotElement

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.SlotElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.PanelElement
public final class SlotElement extends Object implements com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.PanelElement
A registered MKC slot presented as a PanelElement — the keystone of the everything-is-a-panel model. A slot stops being a thing the old slot "decoration" overlay world drew and positioned, and becomes just another element you drop into a panel, alongside buttons and labels.

The two halves of a slot

A slot has always had two separable layers:
  • Registration — a real, server-synced MKCSlot in menu.slots (JEI/EMI see a normal slot). Built at menu-construction time via MKCSlots; untouched by this class.
  • Presentation — where it sits on screen, and its frame/item/hover draw. Historically a per-slot onPrepare reposition callback plus a standalone render helper, both inside the slot overlay world. This is what SlotElement takes over.
The panel already resolves its own screen origin every frame (region anchors, resize, recipe-book toggle — all handled by ScreenPanelAdapter). A SlotElement is a panel-local child, so it rides that origin like any other element: per-screen position becomes a panel property, not a per-slot mechanism. That deletes the duplicate positioning system instead of bridging to it.

Located, not held — the menu-attach lifecycle

A SlotElement does not hold a slot reference; it holds the slot's stable identity (panelId/groupId/localIndex) and resolves the live MKCSlot from the current screen's menu each frame. This is what lets one statically-registered panel work on every screen: the survival inventory and the creative screen carry different slot instances for the same logical slot (creative wraps it in a SlotWrapper and projects it onto a throwaway menu), and a held reference would bind to one and be wrong on the other. Resolving by identity each frame — the same thing the old per-frame reposition scan did — is screen-agnostic by construction.

Why a slot is a click-through HOLE in its panel

A slot's actual item interaction is owned by vanilla: a click flows through AbstractContainerScreen.mouseClicked → slotClicked(getHoveredSlot()), and MenuKit's library-owned getHoveredSlot interception (MKCSlotInput) routes that to the registered slot — making it win over, and so block, the vanilla slot it covers. So the panel must not eat the click; isElementOpaque() returns false (a hole) so the click reaches vanilla. The "block what's behind" is done by that hover resolution, exactly as slots have always worked — the panel here owns only position + render. render(RenderContext) keeps the slot's presentation position current so the hover resolution finds it; SlotElementRegistry tells the library's screen hook which panels currently host a SlotElement, so it resolves them through MKCSlotInput.

      Parameters:
      panelId - the registered slot's panel id (as given to MKCSlots.Builder.panel(String))
      groupId - the registered slot's group id (MKCSlots.Builder.group(String))
      localIndex - the slot's index within its group (0-based)
      childX - panel-local X (within the panel's content area, after padding)
      childY - panel-local Y
